subject: row:songhai-empire
question: When does the Songhai Empire start?
headline: c. 1464, Sonni Ali's accession, whose conquests made the kingdom an empire
definition: The empire starts when the Gao kingdom becomes an empire, not when Gao leaves Mali's hold. One set of dates serves both timelines the row is on (Medieval and Modern States).

kept.location: short description: "Empire in West Africa from c. 1464 to 1591"
kept.note: The article also dates the Sonni dynasty "(c. 1464–1493)" and files the empire under "States and territories established in 1464": Sonni Ali's accession, whose conquests made the kingdom an empire.
The infobox says "c. 1430s", with "Independence from Mali Empire": the end of Mali's hold on Gao, before the empire.

subject: row:kingdom-of-gao
question: When does the Kingdom of Gao end?
headline: c. 1300, Gao's loss of independence to Mali
definition: The kingdom ends when it loses its independence. The infobox's late 1200s and the textbook's 1325 stay as claims.

kept.location: History: "Around 1300, Gao had become prosperous enough to attract the Mali Empire's attention. Mali conquered the city"
kept.note: Loss of Gao's independence to Mali.
The infobox says "Late 1200s"; the body, "Towards the end of the 13th century Gao lost its independence and became part of the expanding Mali Empire."

kept.location: "the kingdom of Mali, which annexed Gao around 1325"
kept.note: The textbook date, tied to Mansa Musa's reign.

openstax-world-history-2.name: OpenStax, World History, Volume 2, section 3.2, The Songhai Empire (Rice University)

subject: event:polish-golden-age
question: When does the Polish Golden Age end?
headline: 1572, the death of Sigismund II Augustus, the last Jagiellonian king
definition: The article's references date the golden age to the Jagiellonian era; the label's broad use to the mid-17th century stays as the 1650 claim. The claims live in pipelines/common/periods.json.

subject: row:modern-states/japan
question: Do the Shogun's holders count as the Japan row's rulers?
headline: yes, across the whole row, beside the rulers the routes find
definition: A row whose head-of-state office has no ruler word in its title and no P1906 link from the polity adds the named office's holders for the whole row. The Tokugawa shogunate's Wikidata head of state names only Ieyasu and Hidetada.

subject: row:medieval/japan
question: Do the Shogun's holders count as the Japan row's rulers?
headline: yes, across the whole row, beside the rulers the routes find
definition: As on Modern States' Japan row: the office's holders are added for the whole row.

subject: row:medieval/papal-states
question: Do the Popes count as the Papal States row's rulers?
headline: yes, across the whole row
definition: The Medieval Papal States row reaches the popes through the office; Modern States' row reaches every pope through its Vatican City phase.

definition: The Emperor was the Yamato Kingship's head (pipelines/ancient/yamato-reigns.json).
